name: Timothy
whenBasis: From Paul's second journey, dated from the Gallio inscription, to his last letters.
summary: A disciple of Lystra, son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father, well spoken of by the brothers. Paul took him on his travels and had him circumcised because of the Jews there. He worked with Paul in Macedonia, Achaia and Asia, was sent to strengthen the Thessalonians and to Corinth, and is named as co-sender of six of Paul's letters. Two letters are addressed to him, left in charge at Ephesus.
body: Paul calls him his beloved and faithful child in the Lord, and writes that he has no one else like him who genuinely cares. The second letter recalls the faith of his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice, and that he has known the Scriptures from infancy. It tells him not to let anyone despise his youth, to drink a little wine for his stomach, and to come quickly. Hebrews says he has been released from prison.

later.text: Eusebius says he was the first bishop of Ephesus; a later account of his martyrdom has him killed there.
Whether Paul wrote the letters to Timothy and Titus is disputed; many scholars date them after his death.
traditions: by Paul: traditional readers and some scholars
by a later follower: many historical-critical scholars
